steps.what: Determine the best layout for the desired tile or stone pattern
Implement the chosen layout by setting out the pattern on the actual surface

tasks.design: Keep layout choice and physical setting-out human, with existing drawings in {DOCS} as reference when available. The setter checks the real surface and implements a pattern that handles edges, cuts and visual alignment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual surfaces and material variation require practical choices that a nominal pattern does not settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native drawings and setting-out tools already support the work.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular boundaries and visible cut positions require on-site judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The setter recognises how the finished pattern will look and adjusts the setting-out to the site.
tasks.altitude: Layout and physical implementation time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Set out a floor finish against real boundaries

evidence.claim: Choosing and implementing a tile pattern requires site-specific judgement and physical setting-out; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is pattern choice and setting-out, excluding quantity take-off, cutting, fixing and cost estimating. Allocate shared site measurement once across tasks.

Client or designer provides the desired pattern through existing project work. Setter observes the actual surface and materials during s1 and produces the set-out pattern in s2; no free structured geometry or correct-layout flag is assumed.
Keep current native drawings and tools. No new model or hardware is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How irregular surfaces and materials are
Whether the desired pattern permits practical edge adjustments
research_questions: Does the set-out preserve the intended pattern while handling visible cuts and site boundaries?

already_counted.description: Choose the layout and physically set out the pattern

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Site judgement and setting-out keep full effort; a digital pattern is not treated as physical implementation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine material quantities from plans and site

steps.what: Study blueprints and examine and measure surfaces and material constraints
Calculate surface coverage and required material quantities from measured dimensions
Determine the final material amount after checking cuts, waste and site discrepancies

tasks.design: Configure a quantity workbook in {SPREADSHEET} using the setter's measured and checked take-off specification. Retain blueprint interpretation, physical examination, allowance choices and final quantity checks with the setter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated coverage and pack-rounding calculations followed the site measurement and design decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: A native workbook can repeat fixed arithmetic from explicit dimensions, material sizes and chosen allowances.
tasks.still_hard: Nominal drawing dimensions may not match the site, and waste depends on the actual pattern and cuts.
tasks.human_edge: The setter knows which site details make a mathematical quantity impractical.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic; physical examination and quantity responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check a material take-off against site conditions

evidence.claim: Explicit surface, coverage and pack-rounding calculations can be configured in a workbook; the proposed task saving is unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is blueprint and site examination plus material quantity determination, excluding choosing the pattern, cutting, installation and price estimating. The checked take-off may be reused downstream but its creation is counted only here.

Project designers produce blueprint versions and suppliers provide material dimensions through unchanged work. Tile setter measures, verifies and captures surface identifiers, drawing version, dimensions and units, opening deductions, selected material coverage, joint assumptions, pack size and chosen waste allowance in s1's 55 hours.

s2 consumes only that checked specification and performs explicit arithmetic. Irregular geometry, missing dimensions, incompatible units or unresolved site differences stop calculation and return to manual determination in s3's 25 hours; the machine does not choose allowances.
Try native workbook formulas before custom code. s3 checks drawing-to-site consistency and practical cuts, not just formula totals; no physical measuring time or system runtime is saved.
unknowns: How often take-offs fit reusable geometry
Whether material coverage and pack sizes are reliable
research_questions: Does the workbook reproduce accepted quantities after site differences and cut allowances are checked?

already_counted.description: Measure and capture take-off fields, choose allowances and check quantities including manual exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain formulas, units and material pack definitions

approvals.approved_version: Exact take-off version, measured dimensions, material definitions, allowance choices and resolved site differences; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=13. Range assumes many irregular areas remain manual and all site examination and practical checks remain; no drawing interpretation saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Help customers select tile and grout

steps.what: Assist customers in selection of tile and grout through discussion and sample assessment

tasks.design: Keep customer advice and sample discussion human, using existing material specifications in {DOCS} where needed. The setter explains practical implications while the customer considers the actual appearance and feel of tile and grout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material choice combines subjective preference with practical site constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Current samples and native specification records already support informed advice.
tasks.still_hard: Lighting, texture, maintenance needs and the intended use can change which combination is suitable.
tasks.human_edge: The setter helps the customer understand a choice in the context of the real space.
tasks.altitude: Advice time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain material choices for the intended space
reach.learn: Customer expectation setting and finish constraints

evidence.claim: Tile and grout selection involves personal preference and practical material advice; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is advice and selection discussion, excluding detailed take-off, purchase ordering, pattern setting-out and installation.

Customer supplies preferences during the conversation; suppliers provide samples and existing specifications. Setter elicits, checks and records the selection within the retained 100 hours; no free structured preference or suitability score is assumed.
Keep current native specification records and samples. No new form, model or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which material constraints matter for the customer's actual site
Whether the selected finish has been viewed under representative lighting
research_questions: Can the customer explain the practical consequences of the chosen tile and grout combination?

already_counted.description: Discuss preferences, examine samples and explain practical consequences

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Customer discussion and practical advice retain full time; no supplier or customer labour is claimed as focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare tile project cost and labour estimates

steps.what: Determine project scope, labor time assumptions and material and rate inputs for estimates
Calculate material costs, labor costs and project estimate totals
Prepare the final cost and labor estimate after checking assumptions, exclusions and totals

tasks.design: Configure an estimate workbook in {SPREADSHEET} and a fixed output template in {DOCS}. The setter chooses realistic labour and cost assumptions and checks the completed estimate before handing it to the quoting role.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated multiplication and total assembly followed the harder scope and productivity decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native workbook formulas can calculate from explicit quantities, rates and selected allowances.
tasks.still_hard: Site access, preparation, pattern complexity and uncertainty determine whether labour assumptions are credible.
tasks.human_edge: The setter recognises work that a simple area-based rate would miss.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated estimate arithmetic; scope and commercial judgement remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess labour requirements against site constraints

evidence.claim: Fixed quantity-times-rate calculations and estimate templates can reduce repeated arithmetic; labour productivity assumptions and the time scenario remain model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing an internal estimate, excluding site take-off creation, supplier negotiation, final quote release and contract acceptance. The take-off is produced by its separately owned task before this estimate and earns no duplicate saving.

Suppliers and shop administration produce existing price and rate guidance through normal work. Setter verifies and captures scope version, quantity and unit, material price and currency, price date, labour hours, hourly rate, explicit allowances, pricing formula and exclusions in s1's 35 hours. Productivity judgement and input capture are retained.

s2 performs specified arithmetic only. Missing prices, mixed currencies, unclear labour assumptions or nonstandard work return to manual calculation and review in s3's 40 hours. No model selects rates or asserts a fixed completion time.
Try native workbook formulas and templates first. Additional rate-field upkeep is counted below; s3 checks whether the assumptions fit the actual scope, not just whether totals add up.
unknowns: Reliability of current prices and labour rate guidance
How much work requires bespoke productivity estimates
research_questions: Does the workbook reproduce accepted estimates without omitting preparation, access or cut-complexity allowances?

already_counted.description: Capture rates and productivity assumptions and check estimate scope, exceptions and totals

incremental.description: Maintain estimating formulas and rate mappings
Maintain additional rate and price fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact estimate version, scope, take-off reference, rates, labour assumptions, allowances and exclusions; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=18. Range assumes many projects need manual adjustments and all scope and productivity judgement remains. Two other-role upkeep hours are outside the focal denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeat quantity and estimate arithmetic may shrink, while site examination, layout implementation and customer advice retain full human time.
reach: Compare practical allowances and productivity assumptions with construction supervisors
Discuss finish choices and setting-out with floor layers
skills_to_grow: Separate calculated quantities from practical waste judgement
Check estimate assumptions against site conditions
role.ambitious_version: Produce traceable quantities and estimates while preserving skilled site judgement and careful physical work.
